extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys (registered before the USPTO), respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO Enrollment & Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements imposed on a practitioner excluded from practice before the USPTO, including immediate effects of exclusion, notification duties, client-file/fund handling, advertising removal, limitations during exclusion, and conditions for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for discipline: disbarment on ethical grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility in that the Respondent was disbarred from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by the Supreme Court of New Jersey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state-court disbarment on ethical grounds constitutes a violation of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5)) and may support exclusion from practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice (ordering of exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded, pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 CFR § 10.133(g), from practice before the Office in patent, trademark and other non-patent law cases beginning immediately upon the Office Director signing the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order effects immediate exclusion under the cited statutory and regulatory provisions; exclusion covers patent, trademark and other non-patent matters before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that the Director of Enrollment and Discipline publish the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will make the Final Order publicly available through its internal publication mechanisms (and also publish notice in the Official Gazette — see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that the Director of Enrollment and Discipline publish the following notice in the Official Gazette: NOTICE OF EXCLUSION [name, registration number, statement that person is excluded from practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 CFR §§10.133(g) and 10.159(b)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice must identify the excluded practitioner (name and registration number) and state the statutory/regulatory basis for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to authorities and bar associations
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.159, the Director of Enrollment and Discipline give notice to appropriate employees of the Office; interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; appropriate authorities of any State in which respondent is known to be a member of the bar; and any appropriate bar association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office must circulate the exclusion to federal agencies, courts, state authorities where the respondent is a bar member, and relevant bar associations as specified in §10.159.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify bars and clients (within 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §10.159(b)(i), Respondent shall within 30 days of entry of the Final Order: a) notify in separate written communications all bars of which Respondent is a member and all his clients for whom Respondent is handling matters before the Office of the exclusion, if any, and b) file a copy of each written communication with the Director of Enrollment and Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must send separate written notices to each bar and each affected client, and must file copies of those notices with the Director within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of active Office case files (within 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.158(b)(2), Respondent, to the extent he has any such files, shall within 30 days of the date of the Final Order: a) surrender each client's active Office case file(s) to each client or to another practitioner designated by each client and b) file proof thereof with the Director of Enrollment and Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active USPTO case files must be turned over to clients or their selected practitioners promptly and proof of surrender must be filed with Enrollment & Discipline within the 30-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of representations suggesting authorization (within 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158(b)(4) and (b)(7), Respondent, to the extent any such expressions or indications exist, shall promptly take any necessary and appropriate steps to remove from any telephone book, legal directory, sign, letterhead, mail or other media all advertisements, statements, representations, and all other expressions and indications that would reasonably suggest that the practitioner is authorized to practice law before the Office, and, within 30 days of taking those steps, shall file with the Director of Enrollment and Discipline an affidavit describing the precise nature of the steps taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All public and printed indications of authorization to practice before the USPTO must be removed, and an affidavit describing the specific steps taken must be filed with the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of unearned funds and client property (within 30 days / proof with petition)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158(b)(8) and 10.160(d), Respondent, to the extent he has any such funds, shall within 30 days of the date of the Final Order return to any client having immediate or prospective business before the Office any unearned legal funds, including any unearned retainer fee, and any securities and property of the client, and shall file a proof thereof with the Director of Enrollment and Discipline no later than filing his petition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unearned retainers, client funds, securities and client property related to USPTO matters must be returned promptly and proof of return must be filed (by reinstatement petition time at the latest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions during exclusion (no practice, no holding out, no advertising, no advice)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158(a) and (b), Respondent, during the period of exclusion, shall: a) not engage in unauthorized practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the Office; b) not hold himself out as authorized to practice before the Office; c) not advertise his availability or ability to perform or render legal services for any person having immediate, prospective, or pending business before the Office; and d) not render legal advice or services to any person having immediate, prospective, or pending business before the Office as to that business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded practitioners must avoid any conduct that could be construed as practicing before the USPTO or representing availability to handle USPTO matters for persons with immediate, prospective or pending business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible paralegal/assistance constraints during exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that in the event that Respondent acts as a paralegal or endeavors to aid another practitioner in any way in the other practitioner's practice of law before the Office during the period of any exclusion directed by the Final Order, Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158(c) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an excluded person assists another practitioner, they must follow the specific rules in §§10.158(c) and (d) governing non-attorney assistance to ensure they do not improperly engage in practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement eligibility and required affidavit (after five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that following exclusion for five years in compliance with the provisions of § 10.158, Respondent may apply for reinstatement to practice by filing a petition for reinstatement and an affidavit showing: a) Compliance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158(a) and 10.160; b) Compliance with the orders of the Supreme Court of New Jersey in a proceeding styled In the Matter of Frank A. Santoro, 192 N.J. 285, 927 A.2d 1285 (2007); c) Respondent acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement, the Director of Enrollment and Discipline will conclusively presume, for limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the stipulated facts, above, are true and (ii) Respondent could not have successfully defended himself against the legal conclusions stemming from those facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires a five-year period of exclusion plus demonstration of compliance with stated USPTO rules and state-court orders, and acceptance of specific presumptions by the Director when evaluating the reinstatement petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court trust account restraint (fact and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of New Jersey ordered that monies, if any, currently existing in any trust account maintained by Respondent pursuant to New Jersey Court Rule 1:21-6 shall be restrained from disbursement except on application to this Court for good cause shown and shall be transferred by the financial institution to the Clerk of the Superior Court, who is directed to deposit the funds in the Superior Court Trust Fund pending further Order of the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-court orders affecting trust accounts (e.g., restraint and transfer to court-controlled trust fund) are treated as part of the disciplinary facts and may affect the practitioner's obligations to clients and the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that all parties shall bear their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order apportions no costs between the parties; each bears their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of stipulated facts and legal conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: ORDERED that the Final Order incorporates the facts and legal conclusion stipulated in Paragraphs 1–11 above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulated facts and legal conclusions agreed by the respondent and OED Director are formally incorporated into the Final Order and are binding for purposes of the Order and future proceedings (including presumptions on reinstatement).
